audit_findings.title: Deferred EASO purchase price may be omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.773 million net liability; approximately $0.03 per share and 0.10% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds unrestricted cash but does not deduct the deferred consideration remaining after its associated restricted cash.
audit_findings.evidence: Total consideration transferred includes $ 30.6 million of deferred cash consideration, all or a portion of which may be paid at least two years after the closing date of the transaction.
audit_findings.explanation: The September 2025 filing reports $28.579 million of deferred consideration and $26.806 million of associated restricted cash. The bridge's $119.699 million cash addition excludes restricted cash, so the alleged gross $28.579 million mismatch is not present. The remaining net claim is $1.773 million, versus $1.862 billion of base equity value, and cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that none of the $26.806 million restricted cash is included in cash and short-term investments, then deduct the $1.773 million net shortfall or document it as immaterial.

audit_findings.title: The FY2024 anchor may capitalize a trough year for fleet reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $89 million year-over-year capex gap, equal to 71.8% of the $124 million OE anchor; normalized adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An understated maintenance-capex deduction inflates anchor OE and therefore every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Capital expenditures decreased by approximately $89 million in 2024 as compared to 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that 2024 capex fell to $51 million from $140 million in 2023, while the company continued operating a large equipment fleet. The $89 million gap is large relative to the $124 million anchor, so even a fraction representing deferred maintenance could materially change estimated value. It is not yet a demonstrated OE error because the record does not separate maintenance, growth and replacement-cycle spending.
audit_findings.action: Build an asset-class replacement schedule using fleet ages, useful lives, disposals and unit costs; calculate cycle-average maintenance capex and rerun all scenarios with growth capex treated separately.

audit_findings.title: EASO's non-controlling interest creates a numerator-claim mismatch risk
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed NCI was $53.139 million and NCI income was $0.505 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated EASO D&A, capex and working-capital cash flows may enter OE at 100% even though common shareholders own only 51%.
audit_findings.evidence: The estimated fair value of total consideration transferred was approximately $ 55 million for a 51 % equity stake in EASO.
audit_findings.explanation: Net income attributable to Hub already removes reported NCI income, but the record does not establish whether every cash-flow adjustment in OE was likewise limited to Hub's 51% interest. The historical reported NCI income is small, but it does not measure EASO's attributable D&A, capital expenditure or working-capital requirements, so materiality cannot be established from the supplied reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Produce an EASO-only OE schedule and multiply each earnings and cash-flow component by Hub's attributable ownership, or value 100% of EASO operations and deduct the separately valued 49% NCI claim.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains a material depreciation-estimate benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $7.9 million of anchor OE, or 6.4% of the $124 million anchor; corresponding base operating-PV sensitivity up to approximately $111 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The useful-life extension raised net income; OE remains overstated to the extent the associated $10 million depreciation reduction was not reversed through an eligible D&A add-back or maintenance-capex normalization.
audit_findings.evidence: These changes in estimate resulted in a decrease in depreciation expense of $ 10.0 million, an increase to net income of $ 7.9 million and an increase in both basic and diluted earnings per share of $ 0.13 , during the six months ended December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The $7.9 million after-tax earnings benefit is filed, but the net OE effect is not demonstrated. A complete D&A add-back would substantially neutralize the accounting change, while the audit indicates some D&A remained expensed. The unresolved portion could be meaningful, but the supplied record does not identify how much of the $7.9 million survived the OE calculation.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild FY2024 OE under the prior useful lives, trace the $10 million depreciation difference through eligible D&A, and rerun the valuation for the unneutralized after-tax amount only.

audit_findings.title: Recurring capitalized technology costs may escape the reinvestment deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $20.9 million capitalized during 2024; omitted amount and valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized software or cloud-implementation cash outlays recorded outside property-and-equipment purchases may be absent from the OE reinvestment deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: We capitalized total implementation and internal-use software costs of $ 20.9 million and $ 16.7 million in 2024 and 2023 , respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes $20.9 million of capitalized implementation and internal-use software costs, while reported 2024 capex included $19 million of technology investments. This indicates substantial possible overlap, but cloud costs classified in other assets could still have escaped the $51 million property-and-equipment deduction. The supplied record cannot determine the missing amount without a cash-outlay reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $20.9 million by balance-sheet classification and cash-flow line to the $19 million technology capex included in OE; deduct only capitalized cash spending not already captured.

audit_findings.title: The dilution ceiling may double-count already-issued restricted shares
audit_findings.magnitude: 1.563824 million-share maximum denominator gap; eliminating the entire gap would raise base value only from $29.69 to approximately $30.45 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Double-counted restricted shares inflate the fully diluted denominator and depress value per share without changing enterprise or equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: During January 2025, we granted 406,585 shares of restricted stock, which includes 111,787 performance-based shares and 258,574 time-based shares, to certain employees and 36,224 shares of restricted stock to our Outside Directors with a weighted average grant date fair value of $ 44.17 .
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation denominator of 62.717334 million exceeds the October 2025 filed cover count of 61.153510 million by 1.563824 million shares. Even the extreme assumption that this entire gap—not merely the 406,585 January grants—was erroneous would raise bull value only to approximately $35.57 per share, still below the $36.68 market price. The finding therefore cannot change the present conclusion, although claim consistency should be corrected.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the transfer-agent count, treasury shares and award ledger, then retain only unissued dilutive awards and performance upside in the denominator.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $42.8 million FY2023 residual; zero effect on the current $124 million capped anchor from the supplied FY2023 amount
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible residual D&A would increase historical OE, but the method caps the anchor at the lower of trend OE and latest-year OE.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2023 $42.8m (23.2% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied residual relates to FY2023. Adding any eligible portion would only increase the historical trend, which is already approximately $193 million and therefore above the $124 million FY2024 latest-year cap. Under the stated MIN(trend, latest) rule, correcting the supplied FY2023 amount cannot increase the anchor or scenario values. No quantified FY2024 residual was supplied.
audit_findings.action: Classify the FY2023 residual for record accuracy, but rerun the valuation only if filed evidence identifies eligible residual D&A in FY2024 or another adjustment that lowers the trend below the latest-year cap.
